cases.title: Sell price auto-calculates from Cost when receiving a special order part
cases.permissions_required: Work order create/edit + order + receive access + See Financial Data (cost/sell fields).
preconditions: 1. Signed in as Admin on the staging build.

2. The organization has a pricing matrix with rules for the Uncategorized category. (The part in this test has no category, so the matrix's Uncategorized rules are what should price it.) Plain note: if the matrix genuinely has NO rule for Uncategorized, confirm with the team what the Sell price should do in that situation BEFORE failing this case.
steps: 2. Create a new line on the work order.
3. Request a special order part: in the New Part Request modal, fill in ONLY the Description and the Quantity — leave everything else empty — then click save and close.
6. On the Receive screen, select the Vendor from the dropdown at the top left side.
8. Add the missing Part Number for the part.
9. Add a Cost for the part (for example 50).
10. Click outside the Cost field and watch the Sell field and the Receive button.
expected: 1. When you click outside the Cost field, the Sell price fills in automatically — calculated from the pricing matrix's Uncategorized category rules (because this part has no category). It must NOT stay at 0.
2. Once the Sell price is filled in, the Receive button becomes clickable (it activates by itself — you do not have to do anything else).

cases.title: Sell price recalculates on every repeated Cost edit on the Receive screen
cases.permissions_required: Work order create/edit + order + receive access + See Financial Data (cost/sell fields).
preconditions: 1. Same setup as SF-RCV-14: signed in as Admin on the staging build, and the organization has a pricing matrix with rules for the Uncategorized category.

2. Run SF-RCV-14 first (create the work order, line, and no-detail special order part; Order; Receive; select the Vendor, add the Invoice Number and the Part Number) so you are on the Receive screen with the first Cost already entered and the Sell price already auto-calculated once.
steps: 1. On the Receive screen, note the Sell price that was auto-calculated from the first Cost.
2. Change the Cost to a clearly different value (for example 100) and click outside the Cost field.
4. Change the Cost a third time (for example back to 50) and click outside the Cost field once more, then check the Sell price.
expected: 1. Every time you change the Cost and click outside the field, the Sell price recalculates from the pricing matrix's Uncategorized category rules — the second and third edits recalculate just like the first.
2. The Sell price never gets stuck at an old value (or at 0) after any of the repeated edits.
3. Entering the same Cost again (step 4) gives back the same Sell price as before — the calculation is consistent.
cases.design_ref: QA lead repro 2026-07-29 (authoritative) — step 10's 'click outside the cost field' auto-calc, repeated. The founder's report specifically says 'no matter how many times the Cost price is updated' — this case covers the repeat-edit half of that report.
cases.notes: Companion to SF-RCV-14; kept separate because a first-edit-works / later-edits-stuck bug is a real and distinct failure mode (named verbatim in the founder's report).

cases.title: Editing Cost in the part edit dialog updates the Sell price and Margin
cases.permissions_required: WO Lines: Create & Edit + See Financial Data.
preconditions: 1. Signed in as Admin on the staging build.

2. The organization has a pricing matrix with rules for the Uncategorized category (same check as SF-RCV-14 — this part has no category, so the Uncategorized rules should price it). If the matrix genuinely has no Uncategorized rule, confirm with the team before failing.
3. A work order line has a part whose edit dialog can be opened (the dialog shows Part Number, Description, Quantity, Source, Vendor, Cost, Sell).
steps: 1. Open the part's edit dialog from the work order line.
3. Change the Cost to a clearly different value and save.
4. Re-open the dialog and check the Sell (and Margin, if shown) values.
expected: 1. After the cost change is saved, the Sell price (and Margin, if shown) update automatically, calculated from the pricing matrix — for a part with no category, from the Uncategorized category rules — the same auto-calc as on the Receive screen.

2. VIU-confirm: whether this dialog applies the same automatic cost-to-sell calculation as the Receive screen has NOT been observed live yet — confirm on the build. Our recorded API fact (part change-request recalculates sellPrice/margin) suggests it does, but that was never turned into an observed test result.

Expected aligned 2026-07-29 with the QA lead's matrix-based auto-calc expectation.

rule28_mini_audit.useful: SF-RCV-14 KEEP (the exact reported failure, now in the QA lead's authoritative 10-step flow; failure = a real reportable bug; the Receive-button gate folded in rather than split — see meta.fold_decision). SF-RCV-15 KEEP (distinct repeat-edit failure mode named verbatim in the founder's report — 'no matter how many times'). SF-VPART-08 KEEP (distinct surface, same default; guarded with VIU-confirm so it cannot assert an unobserved behavior). No MERGE, no CUT; a 4th standalone Receive-button case was deliberately NOT added (would reduce to one gate already covered as a class by SF-VEND-06/C29442 = the over-granularity slop pattern).
rule28_mini_audit.makes_sense: 3/3 SENSIBLE — cold-read check: SF-RCV-14's 10 steps are executable in order from a fresh login (create WO -> line -> no-detail special order part -> Order -> Receive -> Vendor -> Invoice Number -> Part Number -> Cost -> click outside), each expected outcome follows directly from step 10, no invented controls (every label from the QA lead's repro + the screenshot), and the Uncategorized-matrix precondition prevents the domain-nonsense trap of demanding a non-zero Sell where the org's pricing genuinely yields none. SF-RCV-15's precondition (run SF-RCV-14 first) makes its starting state reachable. SF-VPART-08 separates the observed API fact from the unobserved UI behavior via an explicit VIU-confirm line.
rule28_mini_audit.genuine_layman: 3/3 — plain numbered steps a non-technical tester can run word-for-word; traceable to the Fabian 2026-07-29 report + the QA lead's 2026-07-29 repro (ticket placeholder to be re-pointed at the real Jira key per Rule 20).
